The concept

A modern kissaten,
run at Shiba speed.

Tokyo's old kissaten cafés taught us everything: thick toast, hand pours, regulars with newspapers. We kept the ritual — and handed the floor cushions to three very opinionated dogs.

Kissaten comfort

Dark roast pour-overs, cream soda floats, and toast thick enough to stand on. Recipes from a 60-year-old Ginza notebook.

Shiba time

45-minute lounge sessions with the pack. NoLap-naps guaranteed? Never. But belly rubs are on a strict first-come schedule.

Slow mornings

Wood, paper, sunlight. No laptops after 11:00 on weekends — this is a sit-stay-and-sip kind of place.

How a visit flows

45 minutes of pure wag.

STEP 01

Welcome & wash

Order at the counter, sanitize, and get your Shiba-guide card with today's pack lineup.

STEP 02

Floor time

Settle on a cushion. Staff introduce each dog — let them sniff you first, then pet.

STEP 03

Snack & snap

Drinks arrive mid-session. Photos welcome — flash off, treats only from staff.

STEP 04

Sayonara

Stamp your loyalty card, grab beans to go. Same dogs, new stories next time.

No flash · phones on silent Let sleeping Shibas lie Staff treats only · kids with adults
06 / 07
Community & care

Happy dogs make good hosts.

Welfare first

Max 4 sessions per dog per day, two full rest days weekly, and a private garden off-limits to guests. Vet checks monthly — reports posted by the door.

Gentle training

Reward-only methods with a certified trainer. Shy-dog signals taught in every briefing — guests learn to read ears, tails, yawns.

Clean & calm

HEPA air, paw-wash stations, and separate kitchen / lounge zones. 12 guests max per session keeps the room soft-spoken.
